title: Cargo & documents
place: Day 6 · 10:00 · off Port Everglades, cargo control room
goal: Read cargo figures aloud and talk about procedures with the passive.

l20-01.text: Every morning we prepare the cargo report. The figures are taken from the cargo system at zero eight hundred.
l20-01.es: Todas las mañanas preparamos el reporte de carga. Las cifras se toman del sistema de carga a las cero ocho cero cero.

l20-03.text: The volume of each tank, in cubic metres, and the temperature. And the boil-off.
l20-03.es: El volumen de cada tanque, en metros cúbicos, y la temperatura. Y el boil-off.

l20-05.text: LNG is kept at minus one hundred and sixty degrees. A little gas boils off every day, and it's burnt in the engines.
l20-05.es: El GNL se mantiene a menos ciento sesenta grados. Un poco de gas se evapora cada día, y se quema en los motores.

l20-06.text: Tank one, thirty-six thousand one hundred and eighty cubic metres. Tank two, thirty-six thousand two hundred and forty.
l20-06.es: Tanque uno, treinta y seis mil ciento ochenta metros cúbicos. Tanque dos, treinta y seis mil doscientos cuarenta.

l20-08.text: On the report, thirty-two thousand six hundred and ten. But on the screen, thirty-six thousand two hundred and ten.
l20-08.es: En el reporte, treinta y dos mil seiscientos diez. Pero en la pantalla, treinta y seis mil doscientos diez.

l20-09.text: That's a big difference. Four thousand cubic metres can't disappear in one night.
l20-09.es: Es una diferencia grande. Cuatro mil metros cúbicos no pueden desaparecer en una noche.

l20-11.text: Yes. Let me check… The six and the two were swapped. A typing error.
l20-11.es: Sí. A ver… Se invirtieron el seis y el dos. Un error de tipeo.

l20-12.text: Well spotted, Diego. The report is corrected and signed again. Figures are always checked twice.
l20-12.es: Bien visto, Diego. El reporte se corrige y se firma de nuevo. Las cifras siempre se controlan dos veces.

screens.title: The passive: is measured, are checked
paras: When the action matters more than the person: is / are / was / were + past participle.
Reports and procedures use it a lot: The report is sent at 0900. The tanks are inspected every week.
screens.avoid: The volume measures in cubic metres. · The figures are check twice.

screens.q: When is the report sent to the company?

screens.title: Big numbers
steps: thirty-six thousand one hundred and eighty
one hundred and forty-four thousand seven hundred and eighty
minus one hundred and sixty degrees
zero point one zero per cent
paras: thousand and hundred never take -s after a number: thirty-six thousand, not thousands.
British English says and before the last part: one hundred and eighty.
The comma (,) separates thousands; the point (.) is for decimals. It's the opposite of Spanish.

screens.q: Write the volume of tank two in numbers.

screens.title: "Se mide" = "is measured"
paras: Spanish says se mide, se controla, se quema. English uses the passive: is measured, is checked, is burnt.
And on paper: 36,180 in English is 36.180 in Spanish. Read the comma as thousand.
screens.avoid: It measures itself. · Is measured the volume.

screens.title: Long numbers, clear groups
list: thirty-six thousand two hundred and ten
treinta y seis mil doscientos diez
paras: Say long numbers in groups, with a small pause after thousand: thirty-six thousand | two hundred and ten.

screens.why: The others are all about 36,000 m³, and the total doesn't match.
